answer:
HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded, associational): Urban land use in the Barcelona province was associated with specific types of plant introductions — specifically **unintentional** introductions (species arriving accidentally via contaminated seed, global trade, and tourism) and, secondarily and more weakly, **gardening** (ornamental/medicinal) introductions — while **agriculture/forestry** introductions were **not** influenced by urban land.

Evidence (all from supplied data, n=632 plots, associational not causal):
1) SPATIAL — 1000-m buffer, adjusted logistic (presence vs absence, z-standardized covariates: cropland, elevation, road/stream distance, temperature, rainfall, radiation; all models converged): Unintentional presence OR = 26.3 per unit (0→100%) urban cover 2009 (95% CI 6.7–103, p<0.0001) and OR = 79.1 per unit 1956–2009 Δurban (p<0.0001) — i.e., ~1.4× odds per +10 percentage points of urban cover. Gardening: OR = 2.5 (CI 0.7–8.5, p=0.15) and Δurban OR = 3.9 (p=0.12) — positive direction but underpowered. AgriForest: OR = 0.20 (CI 0.01–4.0, p=0.30) and Δurban OR = 0.32 (p=0.56) — no urban association (point estimate ≤1). All-pathway total tracked urban cover (OR = 19.6, p<0.0001).
2) CONTRAST (the core): Unintentional vs AgriForest urban-cover slopes differ significantly (z=2.90, p=0.0038); Δurban slopes z=2.53, p=0.012. Unintentional also differs from Gardening (z=2.51, p=0.012). Gardening vs AgriForest differs in direction but not significantly (z=1.51, p=0.13). So unintentional (and tentatively gardening) introductions are the types tied to urban land; agri-forest is not.
3) TEMPORAL corroboration — pathway×period table (chi2=230, p<0.0001): Gardening became 75.2% of 1985–2019 introductions (era of maximum urbanization, resid +5.0); Unintentional peaked earlier (1901–1984, resid +3.9); AgriForest collapsed (6.1% share, resid −5.5). The pathways associated with urbanization in time match those associated with urban land in space.
4) Robustness — 50-m buffer replicates the contrast (Unintentional OR=5.9 and Δurban OR=6.0, both p<0.0001; Gardening OR=2.0, p=0.07; AgriForest n.s.). Count models (negative binomial, alpha 0.8–1.2; 70% zeros, 441/632) corroborate direction (Unintentional count-OR=3.1) but lack power — the presence/absence logistic is the reliable primary specification.
5) Diagnostics reported as requested: 70% zero-inflation handled via logistic primary (zero fraction 0.698 > NB-expected 0.655 for n.total); all 20 model fits converged (no singular Hessian). Habitat was NOT used as a covariate because it is a proxy for the exposure (adding the 'Urban' habitat dummy — Firth, all converged — absorbs the level effect and reverses the OR to ≤1: n.gard 0.48, n.unint 1.07, n.agfo 0.36; within-Urban-habitat plots show a ceiling/saturation signal, rho=−0.31 for gardening, p=0.011) — a transparently flagged bad-control issue, so the primary models exclude habitat.

Caveat: these are spatial-temporal associations from a single plot survey; "influenced by" should be read as "consistently and strongly associated with urban land cover and with 1956–2009 urbanization", not as demonstrated causation (no longitudinal invasion record, no propagule-pressure measures).

payload.hypothesis: Urban land use in Barcelona province was associated with unintentional plant introductions (accidental arrivals via seed contamination, trade and tourism) and, secondarily and more weakly, with gardening (ornamental) introductions, while agriculture/forestry introductions were not influenced by urban land. Evidence: per-pathway presence/absence logistic models across 632 plots (adjusted for cropland, elevation, road/stream distance, climate, radiation) show Unintentional presence odds rise ~26x per unit urban cover in the 1-km buffer (p<0.0001, also p<0.0001 for 1956-2009 urbanization, ~1.4x per +10pp), Gardening follows the same positive direction but weaker (OR 2.5, p=0.15), AgriForest shows no urban association (OR=0.2, p=0.3); the Unintentional-vs-AgriForest slope contrast is significant (z=2.9, p=0.004) and is replicated at the 50-m buffer. Temporally, Gardening rose to 75.2% of 1985-2019 introductions (chi2=230, p<0.0001) - the urbanization era - while AgriForest collapsed, corroborating which pathway types track urban land. Association, not causation.
payload.workflow: 1) Inspected all four files: plot file (632x37, no missing, n.total=sum of pathway counts, 441/632 zero plots) is the only file pairing pathway counts with urban land; species traits/phylogeny cannot join plots (no species IDs in plot file). 2) Primary unit=632 plots; outcomes=presence of n.unint/n.gard/n.agfo/n.total; exposures=urban cover 2009 and delta-urban 1956-2009 (1000m primary, 50m sensitivity); controls=cropland, elevation, road/stream distance, temperature, rainfall, radiation (z-standardized); habitat excluded (proxy/exposure bad-control, reported diagnostically via Firth). 3) Single-exposure marginal adjusted logistic models per pathway (all converged), effect sizes with CIs, per-10pp ORs, cross-pathway slope contrasts (unint vs agfo, gard vs agfo, unint vs gard). 4) Zero-inflation handled via logistic primary; negative-binomial counts corroborate direction; zero fraction vs NB expectation reported. 5) Temporal corroboration via period x pathway chi-square and standardized residuals. 6) Synthesized single natural-language hypothesis naming the pathway types influenced by urban land use.
